column1: # ============ DENOMINATOR RECONCILIATION — READ BEFORE QUOTING ANY RATIO ============
# An independent derivation found 171 ptrace-only verify candidates against this file's 134.
# THE 37-ROW GAP IS TWO UNRELATED CAUSES, 35 + 2. Neither figure is simply wrong; they
# count different things, and one of them is not a census at all.
#   171   every cell whose verify block has backends_enabled == ["ptrace"] exactly
#   -35   ci = false in that block: present in the manifest, NOT exercised in CI
#   136   ptrace-only verify cells actually run in CI  <-- USE THIS AS THE DENOMINATOR
#    -2   cells appearing in NEITHER bucket of this file
#   134   the figure in the line below
# CAUSE 1, THE 35 — A CORRECT FILTER WHOSE REASON WAS NEVER RECORDED. All 35 excluded
# cells are .c; all 46 non-C cells are ci=true, which is why an independent count agreed
# exactly on the non-C half and diverged only on C. THE FILTER IS RIGHT AND SHOULD STAY:
# a cell not run in CI is not a candidate for enablement work. Only the rationale was
# missing, and an unexplained filter is operationally identical to an accidental one.
# CAUSE 2, THE 2 — AND THIS IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. 134 IS NOT A MEASUREMENT OF THE
# UNIVERSE. It is the SUM OF TWO BUCKET COUNTS: 87 mechanical + 47 needs-judgement, and
# 78 + 56 before the correction. A bucket sum answers "how many cells did I classify",
# never "how many cells exist", so a cell falling out of both buckets vanishes from the
# total and no arithmetic inside this file can reveal it. Two did.
# THE 2 CANNOT BE NAMED, AND THAT IS THE FINDING: the 87 mechanical cells are listed
# here; THE 47 NEEDS-JUDGEMENT CELLS ARE LISTED NOWHERE. A no-truncation search of
# ignored/ and ai_docs/ finds the string "needs-judgement" in exactly one place in the
# whole tree: the single header line quoting the number. 47 of the 134 have no names,
# so 134 is unauditable by anyone including its author, which is why a 2-cell error
# survived: there was never a list to diff against.
# VERIFIED: all 87 rows below are inside both the 171 and the 136. Counts are stable at
# e0536eeb0, ff386d4df, b5b69eb94, d981a4089 and HEAD, so this is not snapshot drift;
# ci_true has never been 134 at any recent commit. NO FIXTURE OR MANIFEST WAS EDITED.
# MECHANICAL CELLS -- the manifest line is the ONLY edit needed (no fixture repair).
# SUPERSEDES the earlier 78-row list. Corrected 2026-08-15: 9 cells were wrongly
# called cannot-fail because the detector matched only `if (ok != N)` and missed
# the TERNARY gate `return ok == EXPECTED_CHECKS ? EXIT_SUCCESS : EXIT_FAILURE`.
# Mechanical 78 -> 87; needs-judgement 56 -> 47. Of 134 ptrace-only verify cands.
# THIS IS A STATIC ESTIMATE AND IT HAS NOW BEEN WRONG TWICE, both times
# UNDERCOUNTING the good set. A MUTATION TEST IS THE AUTHORITATIVE INSTRUMENT
# (see hermit-sabre's empirical exit-gating screen). Do not treat this as proof.
# ================= CAVEAT — READ BEFORE ADDING ANY MANIFEST LINE =================
# "mechanical" answers ONLY: is the manifest line the sole edit? It does NOT mean
# qualifiable. A cell is qualifiable only with a working REFUSE direction.
# TWO DIFFERENT PROPERTIES, AND THEY NEED DIFFERENT MUTANTS:
#   (1) DETERMINISM / parity  -- what `assert = { bitwise_parity = true }` protects.
#       Refuse direction = make the guest's output VARY BETWEEN THE TWO --verify
#       RUNS. Method used for the 7 already asserted: an inert wrapper that keeps
#       the cell's own workload and prepends one run-varying line (a byte appended
#       to a host file that persists across both runs). Confirmed to diverge
#       natively first, so a refusal cannot be a broken fixture.
#   (2) CORRECTNESS / exit-gating -- whether a WRONG-BUT-CONSISTENT guest is caught.
#       Refuse direction = a semantic mutant. Class A cells CANNOT catch this:
#       both runs print the same wrong value, parity holds, exit stays 0.
# hermit-sabre measured (2) on system-utils/startup-surface-identity: the mutant
# bit (ENVCOUNT 121 vs 122, both binaries ran) and the guest STILL EXITED 0. That
# is a true finding about property (2). It does NOT invalidate a parity assert,
# because a real DETERMINISM regression on that cell would make argc/env/auxv vary
# SO: do not screen these with a correctness mutant and conclude the assert is
# inert -- that tests the wrong oracle. Screen with a parity violation.
# Conversely, do not claim a Class A cell gates correctness. It does not.
# class A = emits observed values, no expected-value assertion (parity oracle only)
# class B = asserts expected values and exits nonzero on mismatch (both properties)
# already_asserted=YES marks the 7 qualified at Bar B with BOTH directions measured
# (3 needed a fixture repair first and were Class C, not listed here).
